pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care - Colden Common Primary School
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
Our wraparound care is designed to provide a safe, nurturing, and fun environment for your children,offering a seamless transition between home and school. Whether you need an early start to theday or reliable care after school, we are here to support your family.
Miss Rist is the manager of the provision and lots of our LSAs support the provision in the role as playworkers.
Our breakfast club runs from 7:30am to 8:30am.
Late club runs from 3:15pm to 6:00pm, with the option of a reduced price if collection is by 5:00pm.
Places are limited and will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. We highly recommend booking early to secure your preferred days.
If you have any questions regarding this provision, please contact the team by emailing wraparound@coldencommon.hants.sch.uk
If you are intending to pay with childcare vouchers, please can you let the school know immediatelywhich provider you are with. This means that we will be able to register as a provider with them.
If you are unsure about Tax free child care, please have a look at this website for more information.https://beststartinlife.gov.uk/childcare-early-years-education/tax-free-childcare/how-it-works/
* If you require some wraparound care slots to finish at 5pm and some to finish at 6pm, you will need to book all the 5pm slots separately and then book all of the 6pm slots.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Dinner Information - Colden Common Primary School
pageCache.text:
School Dinner Information
School lunches
Our nutritious school lunches are provided by Cleverchefs, and are cooked on the school site. Any allergies can be catered for and there is a focus on the use of fresh produce. 95% of the ingredients are fresh, which is pretty much everything except peas. If you want to know more about the ethos of Cleverchefs, please look at their website: https://www.cleverchefs.co.uk/primary-schools
All lunches must be ordered in advance, online, by 8am.
There are several lunch options each day, with a rolling 3-week menu. Each option costs £2.75, and payment must also be made online, in advance.

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Years Foundation Stage - Colden Common Primary School
pageCache.text:
Early Years Foundation Stage
At Colden Common, our EYFS curriculum is designed to be broad, balanced, and responsive to the needs and interests of every child. We aim to create an environment where children can develop skills across all areas of learning, building on what they already know and can do. Our curriculum is underpinned by the following principles:
At Colden Common Primary School, our EYFS implementation ensures that children are provided with a nurturing, stimulating, and engaging environment that fosters their development in all areas. We value the individuality of every child and strive to support each one to reach their full potential, preparing them for the next stage of their educational journey. We nurture & enrich each individual child through playful experiences in a warm, safe and caring setting and we value EVERY child’s own individual interests and needs and plan for an enabling environment based on this principle.
Our EYFS implementation is structured around the seven areas of learning and development:
Teaching and Learning Strategies
We employ a variety of teaching methods to support children’s learning:
The content and pedagogy at Colden Common are thoroughly aligned with the EYFS curriculum and framework. We have carefully designed our learning environment, resources, and teaching methods to ensure they support children’s development across the seven areas of learning. Our content is both broad and flexible, catering to children’s unique needs and interests, and is delivered through a combination of adult-led and child-initiated activities.
We are committed to providing continuous professional development (CPD) and support to all of our EYFS staff, ensuring they have the knowledge, skills, and confidence to deliver the EYFS curriculum effectively. For staff who require additional input, we have the following systems in place:
Assessment is an integral part of our practice. We use both formative and summative assessment to monitor children’s progress:
At Colden Common the implementation of our Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum has a significant, positive impact on the development, progress, and well-being of all children in our care. Through a play-based, child-centred approach, we ensure that children are not only ready for the next stage of their education, but also develop key skills that lay the foundation for a lifelong love of learning.
Holistic Development
The impact of our EYFS provision is seen in the holistic development of each child. By focusing on the prime areas: Communication and Language, Physical Development, and Personal, Social, and Emotional Development. We ensure children are confident, independent, and emotionally resilient. Through targeted, personalised learning experiences, children develop:
Academic Achievement and Progress
Our EYFS curriculum provides the solid academic foundation that prepares children for success in later stages of their education:
Literacy Development: Children make significant progress in early reading and writing, with a large proportion meeting or exceeding the Early Learning Goals (ELGs) in literacy by the end of the Reception year. Phonics, storytelling, and shared reading experiences play a vital role in fostering a love of books and language.
Mathematical Understanding: Children develop early numeracy skills through practical, hands-on activities. Many children leave the EYFS able to confidently recognise numbers, count, and understand simple mathematical concepts.
Emotional and Social Growth:
A major impact of our EYFS provision is the development of well-rounded, emotionally secure children:
The impact of our EYFS curriculum is regularly reviewed through ongoing assessment, observation, and feedback. This ensures we are responsive to the changing needs of our children and can tailor our provision to support their growth. Our robust tracking systems highlight children’s progress across all areas of development and ensure that interventions are put in place where needed to support continued success.
The impact of our Early Years Foundation Stage provision is clear. Children leave our setting with the confidence, skills, and enthusiasm to thrive in the next phase of their education. They develop not only academic skills but also important life skills such as resilience, empathy, and independence. Our EYFS curriculum, delivered through high-quality teaching, a stimulating environment, and strong family partnerships, provides children with the best start in life, laying the groundwork for their future success.

pageCache.pageTitle: Class structure and Timings - Colden Common Primary School
pageCache.text:
Class structure and Timings
We have two classes in each of our year groups. Our class structure for the 2024-25 academic year is:
Our school week is currently 32.5 hours, with the compulsory school day running from 8.45 a.m. – 3.15 p.m.
08:45 – 08:55: Registration (children may enter the class at 08:40) 08:55 – 11:40: Teaching sessions (break time to be taken flexibly) 11:40 – 12:45: Lunch 12:45 – 12:50: Registration 12:50 – 14:55: Teaching sessions 14:55 – 15:10: Class assembly 15:15: End of the school day

Remote Learning
Our chosen platform for any remote learning is Google Classroom.
When children join us, they are automatically given an email address that allows them to access all of our online learning tools. Class teachers will make sure that children and parents know what the email address and password is. If you get stuck with this, please contact us and we’ll be able to check the login details and reset the password.
In school, we use the Google Classroom in some lessons.
In the event of learning becoming remote, children will be expected to access Google Classroom and check the learning that their class teacher will have uploaded. Children in Year R will receive communication through Tapestry.

Allotment Group
“We are delighted to announce that Hampshire Garden Trust (HGT) are working with Colden Common Primary School to provide the children with a fantastic opportunity to learn about growing, gardening and the natural world.
During the winter months HGT will be working alongside the CCPS CCSA and Green Team to construct a polytunnel and further improve and extend the allotment area.
Sessions will run every Friday with Project Gardener Jenny Walmsley until the end of October starting up again in March 2025.
We also have an allotment club, run by Mrs Sturges, on a Wednesday afternoon.
Do check out @sowyummyfood on Instagram for more details of Garden Plans for School initiatives in Hampshire.”

CCSA
Welcome to the Colden Common School Association
As parents, you will automatically become part of the CCSA, which is a parent/teacher association run by volunteer parents on behalf of all families and children.
Please ‘like’ and follow the Colden Common School Association Facebook page where we post information about all our events.
What we do
How you can help
The CCSA Committee meet twice per term. There are currently 6 members but we welcome new faces and ideas!
The AGM is held in October and is a great way to find out what events have happened in the previous year, how money fundraised has been spent and plans for the coming year.
Recently, the CCSA has provided funds towards the new KS1 play equipment and revamped the courtyard providing new benches and weather protection.
In previous years new lockers, gardening equipment, library resources, a new inclusive Junior playground, PA system, classroom visualisers, ICT equipment, ipads for every class and even Lego robots have been fundraised for.
Please support us and get involved! : )

Lunchtimes
The lunchtime for EYFS and KS1 (Years 1 and 2) starts at 11.45 a.m. and finishes at 12.45 p.m.
Lunchtime for KS2 (Years 3 to 6) starts at 12.00 and finishes at 12.55 p.m.
The children in Year R and 1 wash their hands shortly before 11.45. Children collect their lunch from the hot food counter and can then take additional bread and salad as well as a dessert. The Year 2 pupils go out to play.
Children who bring sandwiches eat with their peers who are having a hot meal in the hall. If they wish, they can choose to sit outside under the covered courtyard.
We have a class list for all classes so that if any child is missing for their lunch, a member of the hall staff will radio to all staff on duty to find the child and send him or her to the lunch hall.
Children who have a special diet are highlighted on the class register. Their lunch is served on an orange tray to make them and their lunch easily identifiable. If they are allowed bread and salad, according to their special diet, that will be pre-served, along with the dessert that they are able to eat. Two kitchen or lunchtime staff check the provision for children with special diets and sign them off every day.
The lunchtime staff who are on duty in the hall continually pour drinks, wipe tables and direct children to seats. They also encourage children to eat their lunch and children have to ask before they start their pudding, so that there is a check that children have eaten sufficient. The Year 2 children follow the Year R and 1 children. At 12.00, the children in Years 3 and 5 go to eat their sandwiches, Year 3 in the courtyard by the hall and Year 5 in the gazebos on the school grounds. Both areas are covered and have seating.
Children in KS2 who have ordered a hot lunch are called to the hall as spaces become available. Children in Years 4 and 6 who have brought sandwiches are called to the courtyard and gazebos when the hot lunches for their year group are also called.
All children sanitise or wash their hands before eating.
There is supervision on the playgrounds, packed lunch areas and in the dining hall throughout lunchtime, and a member of the SLT on duty in the hall.
At 12.45, the whistle goes in the playground for the EYFS and KS1 children to return to class. The whistle for KS2 children is at 12.55.
